paragraphs: Rabbi Yochanan ben Torta: Yoma 9a (received locator ע׳ א׳), and Jerusalem Talmud there, 1:1. Tosafot Yeshanim there says Pesikta explains that he converted through a cow, and its reading is Rabbi Yehudah ben Torta. Ritva there, in the Jerusalem Talmud’s name, says he was called this because he sold his cow to a gentile, and it refused to plow on the Sabbath until he whispered in its ear. See above, Huna ben Torta and Chanina ben Torta, for the incident at length. Once he came before Rabbi Akiva, who told him: ‘Stand and read from the Torah.’ He replied: ‘I have not reviewed the passage,’ and they praised him: Shemot Rabbah, Tissa, beginning of section 40. In Eichah Rabbah, ‘The Lord has swallowed,’ he told Rabbi Akiva: ‘Akiva, grass will grow on your cheeks, and still he will not come.’ It appears he was early. In the Tosefta, end of Menachot, Rabbi Yochanan ben Torta said: ‘Why was Shiloh destroyed? Because of contempt for sacred offerings.’
